title: U.S. House · California's 7th District
area: Covers part of the city of Sacramento, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

Because California uses a top-two primary regardless of party, both general-election candidates are Democrats. In the June 2, 2026 primary, challenger Mai Vang placed first with 31.2% (65,617 votes), ahead of incumbent Doris Matsui's 29.1% (61,114 votes), out of 210,115 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Doris Matsui
candidates.ballotNote: Placed second, behind challenger Mai Vang, in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Doris Matsui was born in the Poston, Arizona internment camp and earned a B.A. from UC Berkeley in 1966. Before Congress she worked in the Clinton administration's Office of Public Liaison and on the Clinton-Gore presidential transition team.

background.text: Born in Poston, Arizona; earned a B.A. from the University of California, Berkeley in 1966.
Worked as a deputy assistant in the Office of Public Liaison under President Bill Clinton and served on the Clinton-Gore presidential transition team.
Has served as a member of the Smithsonian Board of Regents and as chairwoman of the board of public television station KVIE.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

priorities.text: Campaign site lists economic investment in manufacturing, clean energy and infrastructure; healthcare policy including the Affordable Care Act and telehealth; flood protection for the Sacramento region; and support for seniors' Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid benefits among her legislative priorities.

positions.summary: Says she co-chairs the House Sustainable Energy and Environment Coalition and supports local initiatives on clean school buses and 100% clean energy by 2030.
positions.quote: support many local initiatives on clean school buses and 100% clean energy by 2030

positions.summary: Said only Congress has the authority to declare war and that she would support a War Powers resolution on the strikes on Iran.
positions.quote: only Congress has the authority to declare war

positions.summary: Campaign site says she repeatedly votes no on funding ICE and opposes allowing masked ICE agents to disregard the rule of law.
positions.quote: repeatedly votes no on funding ICE, and opposes allowing masked ICE agents to disregard the rule of law

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Communications and Technology and Energy subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Served as Ranking Member of the Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology during the 2023-2024 session.

candidates.name: Mai Vang
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first, ahead of incumbent Doris Matsui, in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

summary.text: Mai Vang is a member of the Sacramento City Council representing District 8 since 2020, and previously served on the Sacramento City Unified School District board from 2016 to 2020.

background.text: Served on the Sacramento City Unified School District school board (Area 5) from 2016 to 2020.
Elected to the Sacramento City Council representing District 8 in 2020; term runs through 2028.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

positions.summary: Platform calls for Medicare for All and protecting Social Security and Medicare from cuts.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will be a relentless advocate for Medicare for All to guarantee healthcare as a right for every American.

positions.summary: Platform calls for federal protections guaranteeing the right to choose, regardless of state.
positions.quote: We need federal protections that guarantee the right to choose for everyone, no matter what state they live in.

positions.summary: Platform says she will vote to make billionaires pay their fair share and close corporate loopholes.
positions.quote: I'll vote to make billionaires pay their fair share and close corporate loopholes so we can invest that money back into the communities that need it.

positions.summary: Platform calls for funding a Green New Deal to transition the economy to clean energy and for stopping new fossil fuel projects.
positions.quote: I’ll fight to fund a Green New Deal that transitions our economy to clean energy, creates good-paying jobs, and makes sure frontline communities are first in line for investment.

positions.summary: Platform calls the President's tariffs a hidden tax on families and small businesses and says she opposes the tariffs squeezing California producers.
positions.quote: Donald Trump’s illegal tariffs acted as a hidden tax on every working family and small business in our region.

positions.summary: Platform calls for abolishing ICE, ending its funding, and closing for-profit detention centers.
positions.quote: Here’s how we can Abolish ICE

positions.summary: Platform says she will fight to raise the minimum wage and tie it to inflation.
positions.quote: I will fight to raise the minimum wage and tie it to inflation

positions.summary: Platform says she will fight to end military aid that enables war crimes and the occupation of Gaza and will sign onto the "Block the Bombs" legislation.
positions.quote: In Congress, I will fight to end military aid that enables war crimes and the occupation of Gaza.

record.text: Elected to the Sacramento City Council, District 8, in 2020, after serving on the Sacramento City Unified School District board from 2016 to 2020.

sources.title: Gov. Newsom, California lawmakers react to US-Israel attack on Iran that killed Ali Khamenei

researchNotes: Mai Vang has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and no policy-specific content from her campaign website could be retrieved during research, so her stated priorities and positions could not be documented beyond her prior officeholder record.
